title: Congenital Anomalies of Optic Disc and Colour Blindness

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: Morning glory syndrome per the book is a:
opts: Bilateral malformation of the optic disc
U/L malformation of the optic disc
questions.exp: Morning glory syndrome: U/L malformation of the OD. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: Fill up: the cause of morning glory syndrome in the book is a peripapillary scleral defect d/t absence of the ______.
questions.exp: Cause: peripapillary scleral defect d/t absence of lamina cribrosa. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: The fundal photograph of morning glory syndrome in the book shows a large OD with:
opts: A macular star of hard exudates
A radial pattern of blood vessels, spoke wheel like
A champagne-cork surface of the disc
questions.exp: Morning glory photograph: large OD with a radial pattern of blood vessels (spoke wheel like). (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: Fill up: the lamina cribrosa is the fenestrated lamina of the ______ that allows the fibres of the ON to pass through.
questions.exp: Lamina cribrosa: fenestrated lamina of sclera that allows fibres of the ON to pass through. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: Per the book's diagram, if the lamina cribrosa is absent the result is:
questions.exp: If the lamina cribrosa is absent → axial retrodisplacement of the ON. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: A child's disc photograph shows white streaks around the optic disc. Per the book this appearance occurs when:
questions.exp: If the OD acquires myelination → white streaks around the OD. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
questions.q: Which statement about myelinated nerve fibres of the disc is FALSE per the book?
opts: They are a congenital disc anomaly
questions.exp: Myelinated nerve fibres: normal OD is non-myelinated; no visual loss. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — terminology and congenital genetics
questions.q: Match the primary colour with its terminology in the book — 1) Red 2) Green 3) Blue … A) Trita B) Prota C) Deuta
questions.exp: Terminology: Red — prota; Green — deuta; Blue — trita. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — terminology and congenital genetics
questions.q: Fill up: in the book's CB pathology terminology, anopia means ______ and anomaly means a defect in perception.
questions.exp: Pathology: anopia — non perception; anomaly — defect in perception. (Book p40)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — terminology and congenital genetics
questions.q: Per the book, congenital CB is X-linked recessive (m/c) with m > F, the red (L) and green (M) cone genes lie on chromosome X, and the blue (S) cone gene lies on chromosome ______.
questions.exp: Genes affected: red (L cones) and green (M cones) — chromosome X; blue (S cones) — chromosome 7; red ↓ green CB is m/c. (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — terminology and congenital genetics
questions.q: Match the acquired CB cause with the colour affected in the book's table — 1) Optic nerve disease (e.g. d/t ethambutol) — except glaucoma 2) Macular disease — except Stargardt's disease; sildenafil 3) Old age / digoxin … A) Blue/yellow CB B) Red/green CB C) Blue CB: yellowish tinging of vision (xanthopsia)
questions.exp: Acquired CB: ON diseases (eg d/t ethambutol) except glaucoma → red/green CB; macular disease except Stargardt's (a cone dystrophy without CB) + sildenafil → blue/yellow CB; old age/digoxin → blue CB with yellowish tinging (xanthopsia). (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — terminology and congenital genetics
questions.q: All of the following are listed in the book as exclusions in acquired CB EXCEPT:
opts: Stargardt's disease (a cone dystrophy without CB)
questions.exp: Exclusions printed: ON diseases — except glaucoma; macular disease — except Stargardt's disease (type of cone dystrophy without CB); sildenafil listed with macular disease; old age/digoxin. Diabetic retinopathy is not mentioned. (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — types from dichromats to achromatopsia
questions.q: In the book's type tree, a dichromatic patient:
opts: Has anopia for 1 colour but can perceive the other 2 colours
Perceives all 3 colours with anomalies in 1 or 2
questions.exp: Dichromatic: anopia for 1 colour, can perceive 2 other colours (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia — autosomal dominant inheritance). (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — types from dichromats to achromatopsia
questions.q: Fill up: trichromatic anomalous vision (a) protanomaly, (b) deuteranomaly and (c) ______ — the patient can perceive all 3 colours with anomalies in 1 or 2.
questions.exp: Trichromatic anomalous: can perceive all 3 colours with anomalies in perception of 1 or 2 — protanomaly, deuteranomaly, tritanomaly. (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — types from dichromats to achromatopsia
questions.q: Achromatopsia (absent colour vision) in the book's tree includes all of the following EXCEPT:
opts: Total colour blindness with hemeralopia (day blindness)
questions.exp: Achromatopsia: red monochromat (black/white; autosomal recessive; total colour blindness → hemeralopia/day blindness) and cone monochromat (perception of only 1 colour). Deuteranomaly is trichromatic anomalous vision. (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — types from dichromats to achromatopsia
questions.q: Which statement about the inheritance of colour vision types is FALSE per the book?
opts: Dichromatic types are listed with autosomal dominant inheritance
Red monochromat has autosomal recessive inheritance
Trichromatic anomalous types are autosomal recessive
Congenital CB overall is X-linked recessive
questions.exp: Dichromatic (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia): autosomal dominant inheritance; red monochromat: autosomal recessive; congenital CB: X-linked recessive (m/c). (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — types from dichromats to achromatopsia
questions.q: A young man sees the world in black and white and squints in bright daylight (day blindness). Per the book's tree the term for the day blindness is:
questions.exp: Red monochromat (black/white): autosomal recessive, total colour blindness → hemeralopia (day blindness). (Book p41)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: Match the colour vision test with its use in the book's table — 1) Ishihara chart 2) Hardy Rand Rittler test … A) Pediatric age group B) M/c used to detect CB; cannot detect tritan defects
questions.exp: Ishihara chart: m/c used to detect CB; cannot detect tritan defects. Hardy Rand Rittler test: pediatric age group. (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: The principle shared by Ishihara and Hardy Rand Rittler charts per the book is the:
questions.exp: Both charts work on the pseudoisochromatic principle. (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: Per the book's table, the Ishihara chart has ______ plates (numbers and lines, with ↓ false positives and false negatives), and the Hardy Rand Rittler test has ______ plates with shapes (O, Δ, ×).
questions.exp: Ishihara: 38 plates — numbers, lines → ↓ false positives ↓ false negatives. Hardy Rand Rittler: 24 plates → shapes (O, Δ, ×). (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: All of the following are listed colour vision tests in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Tests listed: 3. Holmgren's wool test; 4. Nagel's anomaloscope; 5. Farnsworth Munsell 100 hue; 6. Farnsworth Munsell 15 hue; 7. Lantern test. Amsler's grid (retinal chart) is not a CB test. (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: The most accurate test for the severity of CB per the book is:
questions.exp: Nagel's anomaloscope: most accurate test for severity of CB. (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: A 28-year-old pilot candidate needs the most sensitive CB test, one that can detect all types of CB. Per the book you choose:
opts: Farnsworth Munsell 100 hue test (85 hue caps)
questions.exp: Farnsworth Munsell 100 hue test: most sensitive test; can detect all types of CB; instrument holds 85 hue caps. (Book p42)

questions.sec: Colour blindness — tests
questions.q: Which statement about the remaining CB tests is FALSE per the book?
opts: The Farnsworth Munsell 15 hue test differentiates b/w congenital and acquired CB
The lantern test is used for vocational CB testing
The lantern test uses 85 hue caps
questions.exp: Farnsworth Munsell 15 hue test: differentiates b/w congenital and acquired CB; lantern test: vocational CB testing; the 85 hue caps belong to the 100 hue test, not the lantern test. (Book p42)

units.title: Congenital anomalies of the optic disc
units.guide: Morning glory syndrome: U/L malformation of the OD; cause — peripapillary scleral defect d/t absence of lamina cribrosa; photograph shows a large OD with a radial (spoke wheel like) pattern of blood vessels. The lamina cribrosa is the fenestrated lamina of sclera that allows the ON fibres to pass; if absent → axial retrodisplacement of the ON; if the OD acquires myelination → white streaks around the OD. Myelinated nerve fibres: normal OD is non-myelinated; no visual loss.

units.title: Colour blindness — terminology, genetics and types
units.guide: Terminology: primary colours — red (prota), green (deuta), blue (trita); pathology — anopia (non perception), anomaly (defect in perception). Congenital: X-linked recessive (m/c), m > F (carrier); red (L) and green (M) cone genes on chromosome X, blue (S) on chromosome 7; red ↓ green CB m/c. Acquired: ON diseases (eg d/t ethambutol) except glaucoma → red/green CB; macular disease except Stargardt's (cone dystrophy without CB) + sildenafil → blue/yellow CB; old age/digoxin → blue CB (xanthopsia, yellowish tinging). Types: dyschromatopsia — dichromatic (anopia for 1 colour, perceives 2 others: protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia — autosomal dominant) and trichromatic anomalous (perceives all 3 with anomalies in 1-2: protanomaly, deuteranomaly, tritanomaly); achromatopsia — red monochromat (black/white, autosomal recessive, total CB → hemeralopia/day blindness) and cone monochromat (perception of only 1 colour).

units.title: Colour blindness — tests
units.guide: Ishihara chart: m/c used to detect CB, cannot detect tritan defects; 38 plates (numbers, lines) with ↓ false positives/false negatives. Hardy Rand Rittler: pediatric age group; 24 plates with shapes (O, Δ, ×). Both use the pseudoisochromatic principle. Others: Holmgren's wool test; Nagel's anomaloscope (most accurate for severity); Farnsworth Munsell 100 hue (most sensitive, detects all types, 85 hue caps); Farnsworth Munsell 15 hue (differentiates b/w congenital and acquired); lantern test (vocational CB testing).
